synopsis: Mie theory contributes to lidar weather simulation through scattering-derived coefficients, alongside Beer–Lambert attenuation and probabilistic placement of droplets or flakes that produce false or lost returns [f4507]. Haider et al. extended a ray-traced lidar model with Mie-theory rain and fog backscatter in August 2023; this evidence is on-road [f4506]. The model matched weather-chamber measurements well at low rain rates, but mismatch increased with rain rate and depended strongly on the assumed drop-size distribution [f4413, f4414]. Chapter 8 also describes a Mie-theory rain and fog lidar model packaged as an Open Simulation Interface functional mock-up unit in Sensors work published in 2023, again with on-road evidence rather than demonstrated heavy off-road validation [f6381].

relations.note: Adds a 2023 implementation and packaging example for Mie-based rain and fog lidar simulation.
Weather-chamber agreement at low rain rates supports the model extension.
Qualifies low-rain agreement with increasing mismatch and drop-size sensitivity at higher rain rates.
Provides a dated implementation example of Mie-based weather effects in lidar simulation.
